response.query: How can simulations quantify the effect of varying percentages of missing timestamps on ITS bias and power to set completeness targets like ≥95%?
response.answer: Simulations can quantify the effect of missing timestamps on ITS bias and power by varying the percentage of missing data and analyzing the resulting model performance. Higher percentages of missing data generally reduce model accuracy and power. Setting completeness targets like ≥95% helps mitigate these effects.

results.content: Specifically, we focus on a critical error source of this type of data, tracking undercoverage: researchers’ failure to capture data from all the devices and browsers that individuals utilize to go online. Focusing on individual-level data, while public application programming interfaces (He & Tsvetkova, Citation2023) and data donations (Bosch et al., Citation2024; Ohme et al., Citation2023), have been proposed as options to replace survey self-reports, the most common approach to collected individual-level data on online media exposure is through the use of web tracking technologies. Research has shown that between 53% (Spain, Revilla et al., Citation2021) and 68% (United States, Pew Research Center, Citation2020) of participants in web tracking surveys do not have the meters installed in all the devices they use to go online. results.title: Generative AI for spatio-temporal multivariate imputation ...
results.content: # Research paper Generative AI for spatio-temporal multivariate imputation and demand prediction in water distribution systems. Developed Spatio-Temporal Imputation Model (STIM) for water demand prediction. Introduced Water Distribution Network (WDN) dataset with real-time IoT, weather, and exogenous data. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Spatio-Temporal Imputation Model for Multivariate Water Demand Prediction (STIM). The model integrates spatial correlations and temporal dependencies within multivariate IoT sensor data, employing a generative AI-based imputation mechanism enhanced with Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) and Hypergraph Neural Network (HGNN) modules to accurately reconstruct missing data. The framework is validated using real-world data collected from an IoT-enabled WDN, incorporating both water level and pressure measurements. The model achieves a coefficient of determination () up to 0.90 for imputation and 0.87 for demand prediction, with mean absolute error (MAE) ranging from 0.031 to 0.071 across varying missing data rates. The proposed framework offers a highly reliable decision-support tool for real-time water demand management in IoT-enabled WDNs, even under challenging multivariate missing data scenarios.
